question: A sum of {₹}y amounts to {₹}10,920 at 6\% per annum in a time in which a sum of {₹}12,000 amounts to {₹}15,000 at 5\% per annum, both at simple interest. The value of y is:
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P)₁ = ₹12,000

Amount (A)₁ = ₹15,000

Rate (R)₁ = 5% per annum

Principal (P)₂ = ₹y

Amount (A)₂ = ₹10,920

Rate (R)₂ = 6% per annum

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = A - P

SI = P × R × T / 100

Time (T) = SI / (P × R / 100)

**Calculation:**

SI₁ = ₹15,000 - ₹12,000 = ₹3,000

⇒ Time (T) = ₹3,000 / (₹12,000 × 5 / 100)

⇒ T = ₹3,000 / ₹600

⇒ T = 5 years

Now for the second case:

SI₂ = ₹10,920 - ₹y

⇒ ₹10,920 - ₹y = ₹y × 6 × 5 / 100

⇒ ₹10,920 = ₹y + ₹30y / 100

⇒ ₹10,920 = ₹y × (1 + 0.30)

⇒ ₹10,920 = ₹y × 1.30

⇒ ₹y = ₹10,920 / 1.30

⇒ ₹y = ₹8,400

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**
